articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the January 1994 edition of "SJAA Ephemeris," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It is identified as Volume 5, Number 1, serving as a regular bulletin for the association's members.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: This article announces upcoming club activities including presentations on the Mercury transit by Ernie Piini and Joe Shrock, the start of an Observational Astronomy class, and a call for Board of Director nominations. It also highlights C.E. Optical, a member-run business by Ed Erbeck, offering astronomy equipment with a member discount. The document concludes with a detailed schedule of January and February events, including star parties and general meetings.

articles.title: Finding Planet Mercury From Down Under
articles.summary: The article discusses the November 6, 1993 transit of Mercury across the Sun, visible from parts of Asia and Oceania. Authors Ernie Piini and Joe Shrock detail their early planning efforts to observe and photograph this challenging event, which involved researching equipment needs such as 5-inch telescopes and eyepiece projection systems, and identifying suitable viewing locations. They consulted astronomy magazines and Fred Espenak's article on the transit to guide their preparations.

articles.title: Mercury
articles.summary: Ernie and Joe embarked on a project to observe and record a transit of Mercury, designing and building specialized equipment like a heliostat and a projection system to capture precise timings and images. After extensive testing, they traveled to Canberra, Australia, to view the entire transit, detailing their challenging journey and visits to local astronomical sites like Mt. Stromlo Observatory. The article describes their technical preparations, equipment specifics, and travel experiences leading up to the celestial event.

articles.title: The telescope with eyepiece projection system developed by Ernie Piini (left) and Joe Shrock (right) as setup in October 1993 before departure for Australia. The system consists of: Ernie's simple Heliostat (far left), Ernie's 5-inch double-folded refractor telescope (72-inch focal length) set on top of the shipping crate, Joe's projection unit with screen, and the tripod with two camcorders (far right.
articles.summary: This document describes a specialized telescope system developed by Ernie Piini and Joe Shrock, assembled in October 1993 before being sent to Australia. The system includes Piini's heliostat and a 5-inch double-folded refractor telescope, Shrock's projection unit with a screen, and a tripod with two camcorders.

articles.title: The planet Mercury nears the midpoint of its 6 November 1993 transit near the south west limb of the sun. (time is approximately 3:45 UT). Photo taken with a Celestron C-50, 12mm Orthoscopic eyepiece projection (80X), through a thousand Oaks ND-4 Photographic Solar Filter, using Kodacolor-200 film with 1/250 second exposure. Site: The Greenhills Conference Center approximately 20 kilometers west of Canberra's city center.
articles.summary: This article describes a photograph taken on November 6, 1993, showing the planet Mercury nearing the midpoint of its transit across the Sun's southwest limb at approximately 3:45 UT. The image was captured using a Celestron C-50 telescope with a 12mm Orthoscopic eyepiece and a Thousand Oaks ND-4 solar filter, on Kodacolor-200 film at 1/250 second exposure. The observation site was the Greenhills Conference Center, west of Canberra, Australia.

articles.title: Mercury
articles.summary: This article details an expedition to Canberra, Australia, to observe the November 6th transit of Mercury, recounting the challenges faced with equipment setup, adverse weather conditions (clouds and high winds), and finding suitable observing sites. Despite these difficulties, the observers successfully recorded parts of the transit using backup telescopes and also took advantage of clear nights for astrophotography of the Southern Hemisphere sky. Beyond the astronomical pursuit, the report includes travelogue elements, describing visits to local attractions such as the Canberra Deep Space Tracking Station and other landmarks.

articles.title: Double, Triple, and Multiple stars by Patrick M. Donnelly
articles.summary: Patrick M. Donnelly's article highlights the constellation Andromeda as an overlooked region for observing double, triple, and multiple star systems. It provides detailed observing notes for prominent objects like Gamma Andromedae, a challenging quadruple system known for its color components, and other systems such as Pi, Mu, and Delta Andromedae, along with nearby open cluster NGC 752. The author offers practical tips on magnitudes, separations, and telescope requirements for successful observation, encouraging readers to explore Andromeda's stellar treasures.

articles.title: Creeping wimpism, and frustration
articles.summary: The author, Jack Zeiders, expresses frustration over bad weather and illness preventing him from using a newly purchased 35mm Panoptic eyepiece, contrasting his current lack of enthusiasm for cold-weather observing (dubbed 'creeping wimpism') with past extreme experiences. He also provides updates on club activities, including the rebuild of the club's 14" telescope, plans for a 12.5" Dobson weight reduction, and ongoing discussions about relocating general meetings.

articles.title: SCOPE Version 3.5
articles.summary: Steve Waldee has generously donated 15 copies of his "SCOPE Version 3.5" software to the Association, with proceeds benefiting the Telescope Loaner fund. This IBM-compatible DOS application aids astronomers by calculating magnification, exit pupil, limiting magnitude, and suggests viewing conditions without needing a graphics card or math coprocessor. It features an integrated database of 115 eyepiece types, supports LUMICON filters, and helps plan observing sessions by printing eyepiece performance charts.

articles.title: Internet article re: Eyepiece Magnification
articles.summary: The document features an internet article that clarifies common misconceptions regarding eyepiece magnification and its effect on perceived brightness through optical instruments, distinguishing between extended objects and point-like stars. Following this technical discussion, the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) 1994 calendar is presented, detailing dates for general meetings, Houge Park star parties, and observational astronomy classes.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS is a free classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products or services, with ads running for approximately three months. The listings feature a variety of used astronomy equipment and accessories, including telescopes, mounts, cameras, filters, and observatory components. Ads must be submitted to the editor by the 12th of each month.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: Paul Barton provides an update on the telescope loaner program, detailing the status of various telescopes including current users, due dates, and availability. The article instructs members on how to borrow a telescope or join a waiting list, noting a special procedure for the solar telescope.

articles.title: January 1994
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for January 1994, detailing lunar phases with their rise, transit, and set times, and the positions (distance, magnitude, rise, transit, set times) for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. It also includes solar data, astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and highlights a 'Darkest Saturday Night' on January 8th, all times being Pacific Daylight.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current Offices and Board of Directors for an organization. It provides the names of individuals serving in various leadership roles, such as President, Secretary, and multiple Directors, along with their respective phone numbers.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists the names and contact phone numbers of individuals identified as "Ephemeris Contributors," along with an "Editor." It appears to be a directory of key personnel involved in the creation or management of ephemeris data.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article, 'COMET COMMENTS' by Don Machholtz, reports on the visibility of four comets and the recovery of another. It specifically highlights the discovery of comet Mueller (1993s) by Jean Mueller during the Second Palomar Survey, noting its distant perihelion and potential brightening to magnitude 14 in over a year.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for several comets, including Comet Mueller (1993a and 1993p), Periodic Comet Encke, and Periodic Comet Schwassmann-Wachmann 2. It lists their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation, sky position, and estimated magnitudes for dates spanning from late December to early February. The article concludes with publication information for "EPHEMERIS," a monthly newsletter from the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document serves as a membership application and information sheet for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing various membership tiers—including options with Sky & Telescope magazine and a junior membership—and their respective costs. It provides instructions for submitting the form to the treasurer via mail or in person at an SJAA meeting, along with contact information and notes its status as a non-profit organization from January 1994.
